title: Prefetch-Priming Tension: Lab Brief
content:
Summary:
This note captures a small lab we ran to quantify the tradeoffs between:
 - opportunistic prefetch (background KV/context prefetch before request arrives)
 - session priming (client-driven warm prompts / short primer executed at request time)
Goal: produce quick, reproducible heuristics for product recommendations when to enable prefetch vs require priming for a given session profile.

High-level takeaway (draft):
 - Prefetch reduces median tail (p50/p90) for high-burst workloads with predictable next-turn distributions, but increases steady-state cost ~3–12% depending on cache hit assumptions.
 - Priming (on-request) reduces cold-first-token latency more aggressively for low-concurrency, high-latency-sensitive apps but adds per-request token overhead that inflates cost linearly with request rate.
 - Hybrid: short predictive prefetch + lightweight priming gives best p99 where session continuity is uncertain.

Experiment setup (short):
 - Model variant: open-llm-small-14b-quant (mix of float16 + int8 KV paths)
 - Hardware: 4xA100 equivalent (server pool emulation)
 - Workloads: three synthetic mixes derived from production traces (trimmed):
    * chat-burst (80% short turns [10–40 tokens], bursts of 200 qps for 30s)
    * steady-stream (steady 25 qps, turns 80–200 tokens)
    * sparse-long (5 qps, long turns 500–1200 tokens)
 - Prefetch configs: none (baseline), aggressive (prefetch full last-K KV for top-5 predicted intents), conservative (prefetch only first-block KV)
 - Priming configs: none, micro-prime (10 token primer), full-prime (50 token primer)
 - Measurements: p50/p90/p99 first-token and full-response latency, tokens generated, additional KV read count (proxy for IO cost), dollars/1k queries (cost)

Representative results (condensed, median across 5 runs):

ASCII table: latency in ms, cost = dollars per 1k queries (approx)

Workload | Config             | p50_first | p90_first | p99_first | p50_full | p90_full | p99_full | extra_tokens | cost_1k
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
chat-burst| baseline           | 28        | 84        | 210       | 420      | 640      | 1120     | 0            | $3.90
chat-burst| prefetch-conservative | 22     | 66        | 160       | 400      | 610      | 1000     | +0.2k        | $4.10
chat-burst| prefetch-aggressive  | 20     | 58        | 150       | 395      | 600      | 980      | +0.9k        | $4.35
chat-burst| micro-prime         | 18        | 72        | 190       | 435      | 680      | 1175     | +2.2k        | $4.50
chat-burst| hybrid (cons + micro)| 17       | 52        | 140       | 390      | 590      | 940      | +2.4k        | $4.60

steady-stream| baseline         | 45        | 110       | 240       | 900      | 1350     | 2100     | 0            | $6.10
steady-stream| prefetch-cons    | 38        | 95        | 200       | 880      | 1320     | 2000     | +1.1k        | $6.50
steady-stream| prefetch-agg     | 36        | 92        | 190       | 872      | 1300     | 1980     | +4.8k        | $6.95
steady-stream| micro-prime      | 34        | 108       | 230       | 940      | 1410     | 2175     | +8.0k        | $7.40
steady-stream| hybrid (cons + micro) | 33   | 88        | 185       | 860      | 1280     | 1950     | +9.1k        | $7.60

sparse-long| baseline          | 120       | 240       | 430       | 2450     | 3700     | 7200     | 0            | $14.20
sparse-long| prefetch-cons    | 112       | 210       | 380       | 2400     | 3600     | 6900     | +0.7k        | $14.80
sparse-long| micro-prime      | 40        | 210       | 390       | 2480     | 3750     | 7350     | +60k (tokens primed) | $45.00

Notes on numbers:
 - cost_1k includes baseline compute + token cost (very rough, normalized to internal price tiers). Prefetch cost assumes charged KV reads and occupied memory prefetch amortization.
 - extra_tokens indicates tokens sent as primers or side-effects (prefetch counts as additional reads not tokens but normalized here as equivalent token-cost for quick comparison).
 - sparse-long micro-prime shows huge token inflation because primers were full-document style for long context marking — this is expected and demonstrates priming is expensive when turn-length >> primer length.

Micro-observations and hypotheses:
 - Prefetch pays off when: prediction-accuracy > ~35% for next-turn prefix and when cold-cache penalty (first-token p99 uplift) > ~30–40ms.
 - Priming pays when request rate is low (so per-request token overhead is tolerable) and when the primer meaningfully reduces decode steps (e.g., summarization where primer includes task framing).
 - Hybrid is advantageous for chat-burst: small predictive prefetch reduces the probability we need a heavy priming step; micro-prime can be kept small to capture intent drift.
 - Prefetch-aggressive spikes cost disproportionately for steady workloads because it materializes a lot of KV memory writes that are amortized poorly across low churn sessions.

ASCII cost-latency sketch (p99_first vs cost):

 baseline      |########## (210 ms) cost $3.9
 prefetch-cons |######    (160 ms) cost $4.1
 prefetch-agg  |#####     (150 ms) cost $4.35
 micro-prime   |########  (190 ms) cost $4.5
 hybrid        |###       (140 ms) cost $4.6

Operational notes for productization:
 - UI toggle surface: add 3 knobs: prefetch_mode (off/cons/agg), prime_template (off/micro/full), hybrid_hint (auto/manual).
 - Safety: prefetch must respect data residency + tenant isolation — prefetching cross-tenant contexts must be disabled.
 - Telemetry: instrument prefetch_predicted_intent, prefetch_hit, primer_tokens, additional_kv_reads. Add SLO budget counters for prefetch budget consumption.
 - Cost reporting: expose a prefetch KPIs line item in Console (estimated delta $/month for enabling aggressive prefetch by tenant).

Open questions / next steps (team action items):
 - (Darren) Quick follow-up: run same sweep with quantized-kv-disabled path to measure kernel overhead contribution (JIRA-OPT-2396).
 - (Marco) Validate prefetch prediction accuracy against live intent model (we used a simple Markov predictor in lab).
 - (SRE) Confirm KV read accounting assumptions in billing: do we charge per prefetch read or amortize to session?
 - Product: build small A/B in sandbox to validate hybrid for a customer that mirrors chat-burst (recommendation: 2 week run, target sample 100k sessions).

Unresolved / raw thoughts:
 - Can we do a TTL-aware prefetch that decays aggressive prefetch for low-activity sessions? Would reduce steady-state waste.
 - Consider cheap client-side micro-prime (local short primer before roundtrip) to avoid server token charge — privacy implications to assess.

Appendix: short run command examples (internal):
 - ./run-sim --workload chat-burst --prefetch conservative --model open-llm-small-14b --runs 5 --trace seeds/20280601-chatburst.json
 - ./run-sim --workload sparse-long --prime full-prime --model open-llm-small-14b --runs 3

References: linked artifacts above, internal Slack thread #prefetch-priming-jun28, and PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/pr/prefetch-experiments-12 (experiment harness).

Draft ends — feedback welcome.
